findings.title: Compliance metrics count retained metadata as live objects after byte expiry
findings.reachable_path: A successful services_retention._complete leaves EvidencePhoto intact and writes EvidenceObjectRetentionState.EXPIRED. reports._live_buckets still increments object_live_count for that photo and sets object_expired_count to zero. Newly finalized rollups use the same constants.
findings.impact: Live and recomputed compliance output misrepresents expired bytes as live.
findings.required_resolution: Specify creation-time history versus current retained-object state, including the meaning of bytes. Preserve append-only historical revisions; define how current metrics remain correct for older rolled buckets. Cover actual byte expiry, issue/return partitions and tenant scope.
findings.test_evidence_limit: operations/test_report_coverage_rollups.py:116-149 deletes photo rows through the maintenance gate. evidence/test_retention_rollup_boundaries.py:39-61 exercises mocked expiry but asserts only that an existing rollup is unchanged. Neither establishes correct current live/expired report metrics.

findings.title: Expiry claims do not revalidate a newly committed retention policy
findings.reachable_path: The sweep snapshots candidate IDs and policy_days once. Before a later candidate is claimed, a manager can commit update_policy increasing retention, for example from 30 to 365 days. _claim reloads the photo but never reloads policy or checks created_at against a fresh cutoff. The sweep deletes that candidate using the old snapshot.
findings.impact: Evidence bytes can be irreversibly deleted although the longer policy committed before their expiry claim.
findings.boundary: The tenant source boundary uses shared coordination; it does not serialize ordinary policy updates against the sweep. No runtime interleaving was executed.

findings.title: Expiry can subtract uncharged, client-declared bytes from unrelated managed storage
findings.reachable_path: An authorized upload-URL request creates a photo with caller-supplied size_bytes before any upload or finalization. If no upload occurs, both object HEADs later return missing. The sweep falls back to recorded_size. With no finalization row, _complete treats quota_was_charged as true even in PUT mode and calls free_storage with that declared amount.
findings.impact: Expiry of an unuploaded photo can reduce storage_bytes_used for other objects, potentially to zero, weakening managed quota enforcement. This requires managed mode and an enabled sweep after the retention window.
findings.boundary: Terminal-state idempotence prevents repeated subtraction for one row, but does not prove that the first subtraction corresponds to a charge. No provider or counter behavior was executed.

findings.title: Skipping an active finalizer leaves a committed expiry blocker
findings.reachable_path: For an eligible photo with a fresh PROMOTING finalization and no retention row, _claim creates an EXPIRING retention row before checking the finalizer. It then returns None normally, committing that new row without a claim token. The finalizer can finish, but the consuming workflow's lock_evidence_for_attachment returns false because any retention row exists.
findings.impact: A sweep that reports the photo as skipped can nevertheless reject the in-flight issue or return attachment and leave it blocked pending subsequent retention processing.
findings.boundary: The source-confirmed case uses an already eligible photo being finalized concurrently; no PostgreSQL interleaving was executed.

findings.title: Evidence upload and detail omit staff-origin tenant admission
findings.reachable_path: With API_CLIENT_AUTH_REQUIRED false and no opted-in HMAC credentials, an active staff_api actor authorized in spaces A and B can send an Origin-A request targeting B's upload URL or evidence detail. Upload checks HasMakerspaceAction; detail checks active authentication and actor-wide action scope. Neither invokes staff_origin_scope_allows or an equivalent origin restriction. JWT staff_api admission does not apply the staff-social origin validator.
findings.impact: A tenant frontend can obtain another authorized tenant's private evidence URL or create its upload metadata through the same actor session, violating the repository's origin-to-tenant boundary.
findings.boundary: This does not bypass the actor's RBAC membership scope. It bypasses the additional browser-origin restriction. Retention settings use IsActiveStaff and do apply that restriction.
